text: Use when a website targets a named professional or buying-committee member, or a person-level page only changes the name, title or salutation of an account page.
note: Site: "Never name people at the account"; no contact research in the workspace. A page for one person cannot be built today.

text: Establish their exact employer and supplied contact entity ID. When exposed, use `read_claims(entity_id=<resolved contact ID>, ...)` for relevant professional statements … Account overview alone is not a contact read.

Prefer the person's own eligible, sourced professional criterion; next use a documented responsibility. A title alone supports role-relevant framing, not their private priorities, feelings or buying authority.
Record: person/employer; supporting excerpt and status; responsibility/criterion; question they need to resolve; seller mechanism; demonstration; actual next action.
Compared with the account page, something substantive must change: explanation, priority, depth or evidence. A greeting plus the same feature tour is not person-level work.

Their name need not be the headline or a navbar label. A discreet eyebrow can identify the intended reader; the headline explains the professional value. Use authentic portraits only when available … do not synthesize a named person.
Do not use private or sensitive interests, inferred emotional pressure, assumed budget authority or an unrelated hobby to manufacture depth.

Before composition, compare account and contact briefs side by side. Can you name the professional evidence that changed the page? If not, report a role-relevant draft rather than pretending it is deeply person-specific.

The personal statement selects the demonstration and questions. It does not establish that ownership is currently broken, that Morgan controls budget or wants a rapid win. Do not say "we know you struggle with handoffs."
